lessons.culture: In Cairo a cup of coffee or tea is the first gesture of hospitality, at home and at the ahwa (coffee shop). Turkish-style coffee is ordered by sugar level: saada (none), mazbooT (medium) or sukkar ziyaada (extra), and tea often comes in a glass with mint.

lessons.culture: Cairo menus are usually printed in Arabic and English, and waiters happily recommend dishes. Koshari, ful and Ta3meyya (falafel) are everyday Egyptian dishes made without meat, so they are the usual answer to a vegetarian question.

lessons.culture: Friends in Cairo often argue over who pays, saying 'el-7isaab 3aleyya' (the bill is on me) with real insistence, and refusing once or twice is polite. Many restaurants add a service charge (khidma) to the bill, and a little extra for the waiter is still common.

challenge.title: At the Cairo Restaurant
challenge.instructions: Say a full conversation in Egyptian Arabic at a restaurant in Cairo. Ask for a recommendation, order a drink and a dish with one preference, then ask for the bill and close the meal politely.
required_elements: Ask what is on the menu or what the waiter recommends
Order at least one drink and one dish, including one preference (for example no onion, extra bread, or sugar level)
Ask for the bill and how much it is
Close the meal with a thank-you or a compliment to the food
